messages:
jamal: Hey all — emergency. Primary for EU weekend (sophie's shift) just had a family emergency and can't take the overnight window starting in ~30m. I tried the usual swap list first. No volunteers yet. Can someone pick up primary or we need to do a bridged handoff?

sophie: Ugh, sorry team. I can do an overlap for 15m to hand off notes then sign out. Can't stay for the full overnight. Leaving my checklist in the runbook link below.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2042 — Hosted API errors (Sev2). Paging primary: @sophie. If primary unavail, escalate to secondary.

jamal: Also, heads up, INC-2042 just paged earlier — customers reporting 502s for generation endpoints in eu-west. I already opened a bridge and put notes in the incident doc. If we don't get a full primary overnight, we need a primary who can own the bridge and coordinate with SRE.

alex: I can take primary starting now for the next 6 hours (00:30-06:30 UTC). Can overlap with sophie for handoff. I can also be on the bridge.

maria: I can be secondary and monitor metrics + paging. If alex needs me to swap in, ping me on SMS.

jamal: Awesome — alex = primary, maria = secondary. Sophie, please paste any runbook pointers you used and the short checklist.

sophie: Cool — paste below. Quick checklist: 
1) Confirm error rate and affected routes: Grafana -> Redwood / Hosted API / eu-west -> Errors panel
2) Check pods: `kubectl -n hosted get pods -l app=hosted-api`
3) Tail logs for 502 spikes: `kubectl -n hosted logs -l app=hosted-api --since=10m`
4) If KV cache pressure, trigger cache flush for the shard (only if safe): `curl -X POST https://internal-admin/eu/cache/flush -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\"`
5) Fallback: flip routing to model-compact (rollout flag) if tail latency high — see runbook step 4
6) Notify support with the status update template in the incident doc

sophie: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hosted-api-degradation (section 3 for model fallback)

ops-bot: Bridge created: https://bridge.redwood.internal/bridges/INC-2042

alex: On it. Joining bridge and looking at logs now. First glance: increased 502s correlate with a surge of long-running requests and a couple of slow inference workers timing out. Spinning up additional dsp-worker pool might help.

maria: I'm watching SLO dashboard. Error rate spiked at 00:12 UTC, currently 3.4% 5m error rate on /generate. Latency p95 up from 180ms to 1.2s.

alex: Quick mitigation plan I'm executing: 
- Increase worker pool for model-serving eu-west by +2 (hotfix autoscaler override)
- Temporarily enable model-compact fallback for the most-requested route (10% traffic, will increase if stable)
- Post quick status update to support then loop in customer success if it stays >2% for 15m

alex: Commands I'm running now: 
```
# override autoscaler for eu-west serving pool
kubectl -n serving patch hpa hosted-api-eu --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":6}]'
# enable 10% rollout of model-compact on route /generate
redwoodctl rollout set --route /generate --variant model-compact --percent 10 --region eu-west
```

jamal: Good. Remember: do not flush KV unless we confirm cache pressure, that can increase latency. If you need to flip full traffic to model-compact, follow the canary steps in runbook.

alex: Understood. Patch applied and rollout command issued. Monitoring metrics...

maria: Metrics trending down slightly. Error rate 2.1% now. P95 760ms. Still above SLO but improving.

oncall-bot: Paging policy reminder: if primary unresponsive for 10m during a Sev2, escalate to on-call manager @jamal.

jamal: We're good on ownership. Alex, please take the incident doc owner tag and add the short-term actions and time boxed checks (15m, 45m). Sophie— leaving any last notes?

sophie: Left the exact run commands and my local note about a flaky nvidia node we saw last week (node-az3-gpu-07). If you end up needing to cordon it, the runbook has cordon/drain steps.

alex: Noted. I see node-az3-gpu-07 with higher OOM kills historically, but not in the last 2h. If it starts spiking, I'll cordon it and spin up replacements.

maria: If we need follow-on coverage after 06:30 UTC, I can extend until 08:00 but need a heads-up 45m before to reorganize my morning.

jamal: Copy. If needed we'll rotate. For now marking roster: alex primary (00:30-06:30 UTC), maria secondary (monitoring/sms), sophie overlapping handoff (00:15-00:30). I'll update the oncall schedule doc and notify support.

alex: Leaving quick checklist in incident doc and will post a support status in 10m. If anyone wants to subscribe to the bridge, link above.

maria: Subscribed. Also FYI for next time — add a short section in the runbook about last-minute primary swaps (how to transfer bridge ownership + pager contacts). That would make these handoffs cleaner.

jamal: Agreed. I'll add a PR to the runbooks repo after this. Thanks everyone, and alex — reach out if you need immediate help on the bridge.

alex: Will do. Updating incident doc now.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2042 status updated: mitigations in progress.

jamal: Thanks team. Will follow up in the morning with a short post-incident note and whether we need a follow-up postmortem.

sophie: Thanks — and sorry for the disruption. Appreciate the quick cover. :heart:

alex: No worries. Team handled it.

maria: Backups: @oncall-bot, please DM me if paging resumes after 06:00 UTC and alex is unresponsive.

oncall-bot: DM rule configured for maria for incidents with open pager after 06:00 UTC.

jamal: Thread closing for now — will re-open if anything changes.
